# Introduction | Developer Docs

The Figma MCP server brings Figma into your AI workflow. It gives AI agents the design context they need to generate code from your Figma files, and lets agents write native Figma content back to the canvas.

MCP servers use the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/introduction), a standard interface that lets AI agents interact with data sources.

## What you can do with the Figma MCP server[​](#what-you-can-do "Direct link to What you can do with the Figma MCP server")

*   **Let your agent write directly to the canvas in Figma Design, FigJam, and Figma Slides**
    
    Create and modify native Figma content from your MCP client. With the right skills, agents can build and update frames, components, variables, and auto layout in your files, using your design system as the source of truth.
    
    note
    
    **Note:** This feature requires the [remote Figma MCP server](/docs/figma-mcp-server/remote-server-installation/) and a Full seat to write outside your drafts. It's free during the beta period and will eventually become a usage-based paid feature.
    
    [Learn more about writing to the canvas](/docs/figma-mcp-server/write-to-canvas/)
    
*   **Generate designs from the live UI of your web apps and sites**
    
    Turn live UI from your browser (production, staging, or localhost) into editable design layers. Send pages, elements, or whole flows to Figma Design for exploration, alignment, and refinement.
    
    [Learn more about generating designs from your interfaces](/docs/figma-mcp-server/code-to-canvas/)
    
*   **Generate code from selected frames**
    
    Select a Figma frame and turn it into code. This is useful for product teams building new flows or iterating on app features.
    
*   **Extract design context**
    
    Pull variables, components, and layout data into your IDE. This is especially useful for design systems and component-based workflows.
    
*   **Retrieve FigJam resources**
    
    Use content from your FigJam diagrams in your code generation workflow, so early-stage ideas, flows, and architecture maps carry into development.
    
*   **Retrieve Make resources**
    
    [Gather code resources from Make files](/docs/figma-mcp-server/bringing-make-context-to-your-agent/) and provide them to your agent as context. This helps as you move from prototype to production.
    
*   **Keep generated code consistent with Code Connect**
    
    Improve output quality by reusing your actual components. Code Connect keeps generated code consistent with your codebase.
    
    [Learn more about Code Connect](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/23920389749655-Code-Connect)
    
*   **Give your agent project context with Figma Specs**
    
    Use the `figma-spec` skill to let your agent read, create, and update your team's specs. Share requirements before your agent starts building, and have it capture decisions and discoveries back in the spec as it works.
    
    **Note:** Figma Specs is in open beta. Writing to a spec requires the [remote Figma MCP server](/docs/figma-mcp-server/remote-server-installation/) and edit access to the file.
    
    [Learn more about the figma-spec skill](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/39166810751895#figma-spec)
    

Write to canvas and code to canvas are continuously being improved. If you run into issues, report them using [Fig, our support chatbot](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/360041057214-Explore-Figma-s-help-and-support-resources#h_01KBJZP4HEVHZSHXBV6PFQBPH0), or by [emailing support (paid plans)](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/360041057214-Explore-Figma-s-help-and-support-resources#h_01KBJZP4JHXDEZM922NWPF3P9D).

## Set up the MCP server[​](#how-to-connect "Direct link to Set up the MCP server")

You can connect to the Figma MCP server in two ways:

*   **Remote MCP server (recommended)**: Connects directly to Figma’s hosted endpoint at `https://mcp.figma.com/mcp`, without the Figma desktop app. The remote server offers the broadest set of features and is the best choice for most users. [Learn how to install the remote MCP server.](/docs/figma-mcp-server/remote-server-installation/)
*   **Desktop MCP server**: Runs locally through the [Figma desktop app](https://www.figma.com/downloads). The desktop server is intended for specific organization and enterprise needs. It requires a Dev or Full seat on a Professional, Education, Organization, Government, or Enterprise [plan](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/360040328273). [Learn how to install the desktop MCP server.](/docs/figma-mcp-server/local-server-installation/)

For information about usage and rate limits, see [Plans, access, and permissions](/docs/figma-mcp-server/rate-limits-access/#rate-limits).

note

Figma for Government supports the desktop server only. See [Figma for Government](/docs/figma-mcp-server/local-server-installation/#figma-for-government) for available tools and current limitations.

If you plan to write to the canvas, also install [Figma’s skills](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/39166810751895) for your MCP client. Skills help your agent use the write tools more reliably and follow the right workflow when creating or updating content in Figma.

### Connect the MCP server to your editor[​](#h_01K25F7RBRZKCATVJHNXCS6KXW "Direct link to Connect the MCP server to your editor")

Follow the instructions for your editor to connect to the remote or desktop server. Some clients also support [skills](#h_01KG5HNM2M3Y6RGBRK84FH1Z1E), which add agent-level instructions that help AI tools work more effectively with Figma designs.

Who can use this feature

*   Professional, Education, Organization, and Enterprise [plans](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/360040328273)
*   [Figma Design](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/15297425105303), [FigJam](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/15300412458647), and Figma Slides
*   Requires edit access to the file
*   Requires a [supported MCP client](/docs/figma-mcp-server/#h_01K25F7RBRZKCATVJHNXCS6KXW) connected to the remote Figma MCP server

Writing to the canvas is currently in beta and free to use during the beta period. It will eventually become a usage-based paid feature.

With the Figma MCP server, you can prompt your agent to create and edit content directly in your Figma files. Instead of describing a layout in chat and rebuilding it by hand, your agent builds real Figma content: frames, components, variants, variables, and auto layout.

This works especially well with design systems. Your agent can build with the components, variables, and layout rules your team already uses, instead of drawing shapes that only look right. The result is standard, editable Figma content that's easy to review, refine, and build on, with your design system as the source of truth from canvas to code.

Writing to the canvas is different from [sending UI to Figma](/docs/figma-mcp-server/code-to-canvas/). Sending UI to Figma captures a running app as flat layers, without a connection to your libraries. Writing to the canvas builds with your existing components and variables. You can use them together: capture your latest UI, then have your agent refine it with your design system.

For an overview, read [The Figma canvas is now open to agents](https://www.figma.com/blog/the-figma-canvas-is-now-open-to-agents/) on the Shortcut blog.

## How it works[​](#how-it-works "Direct link to How it works")

Your agent writes to the canvas with the [`use_figma`](/docs/figma-mcp-server/tools-and-prompts/#use_figma) tool. The tool lets your agent run code in your Figma file through the [Figma Plugin API](https://developers.figma.com/docs/plugins/), so it can create and update real design structure rather than a screenshot or static export.

tip

Install [Figma's skills](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/39166810751895) for your client. The `figma-use` skill helps your agent use `use_figma` reliably and follow the right workflow. Depending on your client, your agent may load it automatically before writing to a file.

Your agent can also read and write **Figma Specs** with the `figma-spec` skill. Share requirements and project context with your agent before it builds, then have it capture decisions and discoveries back in the spec as it works. Figma Specs is in open beta.

## Write to the canvas[​](#get-started "Direct link to Write to the canvas")

1.  [Set up the remote Figma MCP server](/docs/figma-mcp-server/remote-server-installation/) for your client.
    
2.  Open the Figma Design file you want to work in and copy a link:
    
    *   To work in the whole file, copy the URL from your browser's address bar.
    *   To work on a specific layer, right-click it and select **Copy link to selection**.
    
    The remote server uses links to know which file or layer to work with.
    
3.  Paste the link into a prompt that tells your agent what to do. For example:
    
    *   "Using this Figma file: <Figma file URL>, create a new page and build a settings screen with auto layout using our existing components."
    *   "Using this selection: <link to selection>, convert these raw values to variables and update the surrounding components to use them."
    *   "Using this Figma file: <Figma file URL>, add a new empty state that matches the existing design system."
    
    Your agent looks at the file to learn its structure and conventions, then makes the changes.
    
4.  Open the file in Figma to review the result. Then keep prompting your agent to refine it or keep building.
    

caution

Because this feature is in beta, test on a duplicate of your library or a draft file before changing production files, and keep a backup copy.

## Tips for better results[​](#tips "Direct link to Tips for better results")

*   **Include a link.** Put the file URL or a link to your selection in your prompt so your agent knows exactly where to work.
*   **Keep going in the same conversation.** After your first prompt, your agent usually assumes you want to keep working in the same file. For example, after "Using this file: <Figma file URL>, create a profile settings screen," you can follow up with "Add an empty state below that" or "Now convert the color values in this section to variables."
*   **Make large changes in steps.** Your agent works best when it reviews the file first, then creates or updates variables, components, and layouts in smaller steps, checking its work as it goes.
*   **Name what to use.** When working with a design system, mention the libraries, components, variables, or modes you want your agent to use. You'll get the best results when your agent builds with what already exists in the file.

## Current limitations[​](#limitations "Direct link to Current limitations")

*   Each tool call can return up to 20 KB of output.
*   `use_figma` can't add new images on its own. Your agent adds images with [`upload_assets`](/docs/figma-mcp-server/tools-and-prompts/#upload_assets), and can create new ones with [`generate_image`](/docs/figma-mcp-server/tools-and-prompts/#generate_image). Importing components that contain images or videos, and creating GIFs, aren't supported yet.
*   Fonts must be [uploaded to your Figma account](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/360039956894-Add-a-font-to-Figma). Fonts that are only installed on your computer aren't available.
*   Components must be published manually before Code Connect mappings can be completed.
*   Output is beta quality and may need manual review and cleanup.

Writing to the canvas is being improved continuously. If you run into issues, report them using [Fig, our support chatbot](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/360041057214-Explore-Figma-s-help-and-support-resources#h_01KBJZP4HEVHZSHXBV6PFQBPH0), or by [emailing support (paid plans)](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/360041057214-Explore-Figma-s-help-and-support-resources#h_01KBJZP4JHXDEZM922NWPF3P9D).

For more questions, see the [Figma MCP server FAQs](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/39252411778583).

content.text:
Skills are pre-built instructions that teach your AI agent how to handle common Figma tasks reliably, such as creating a new file, building a screen from your design system, or generating code from a design. Without skills, you'd need to describe each step yourself every time. With them, you can ask your agent to do something like "create a new Figma file" or "implement this design" and it already knows what to do.

**Note:** This article describes the skills that Figma provides for the Figma MCP server. To learn about MCP skills and how to use them, check out [Use skills with the Figma MCP server](/hc/en-us/articles/39287396773399).

Figma provides a number of skills for use with the [Figma MCP server](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/39216419318551):

*   [figma-use](#h_01KMFHKFDR8Q78CR8CC9W8J18E)
*   [figma-use-figjam](#h_01KPXSNCM35QC8ZJFJVASXJG50)
*   [figma-use-slides](#h_01KS0S2X0EDWC8MRRS1BE16QP9)
*   [figma-swiftui](#h_01KTM69WDPTM2RTB3JKJ3HYNYN)
*   [figma-code-connect](#h_01KMFHKFDRME0YHTRCJ6J4Q2J4)
*   [figma-create-new-file](#h_01KMFHKFDR3V4PCCPPH4NHG1PP)
*   [figma-generate-diagram](#h_01KS0S2X0EJ0XBCAHPRTKYTXD1)
*   [figma-code-workflows](#figma-code-workflows)
*   [figma-spec](#figma-spec)

As well as two example skills that demonstrate how to write to the canvas in Figma:

*   [figma-generate-library](#h_01KMFHKFDRH9CCNEFBDKEJ3MQS)
*   [figma-generate-design](#h_01KMFHKFDRN7C0PSVAB88Z8087)

Additionally, you can browse a collection of [curated skills in GitHub](https://github.com/figma/community-resources/tree/main/agent_skills).

## Get the Figma skills

### Figma plugin

The easiest way to get the Figma skills is through an agentic tool that supports the Figma plugin, such as Claude Code or Cursor. When you install the Figma plugin in one of these tools, the skills are included automatically.

The instructions for [setting up the remote Figma MCP server](https://developers.figma.com/docs/figma-mcp-server/remote-server-installation/) describe how to get the Figma plugin for several common clients.

### Download the skills

If your AI tool doesn't have a Figma MCP plugin, you can download and manually install the skills.

[Click here to download the skills.](https://github.com/figma/mcp-server-guide/archive/refs/heads/main.zip)

You can also view the skills in our [mcp-server-guide repository](https://github.com/figma/mcp-server-guide) on GitHub.

Once you've downloaded the skills, the easiest way to install them is to ask your AI agent to unzip the file and place the contents in the right folder for your tool. Your agent will know where skills are expected to live.

### Troubleshooting

If you run into issues downloading or installing skills, see our [Figma MCP server FAQs](/hc/en-us/articles/39252411778583).

## Use skills

You use the Figma skills for the MCP server the same way skills are generally used with Claude Code, Codex, and others. The exact way you invoke a skill depends on the client.

To learn more, see [Use skills with the Figma MCP server.](/hc/en-us/articles/39287396773399)

## Figma skills

This article dives into the skills that Figma provides and some example use cases, but don't think of the examples as the limits of a skill; they're just a way to get started!

The skills you'll use depend on the task you're doing.

`figma-use`, for example, is the foundational skill for anyone who wants to write content to a Figma canvas. The skill is used for creating frames, components, variables, and layouts directly in a file. Other skills build on top of it for more specific workflows.

Some skills, like `figma-create-new-file` and `figma-generate-design`, are useful for designers working directly with Figma files.

Others, like `figma-code-connect` and `figma-code-workflows`, are more relevant if you write code or are working closely with developers.

And `figma-spec` helps your whole team share project context with agents, so everyone builds from the same requirements.

### figma-use

`figma-use` is the skill that powers write-to-canvas. When you want your agent to create or modify content directly in a Figma file, such as building frames, placing components from your design system, setting up variables, arranging auto layout, this is the skill that makes it possible.

Instead of generating a static image or a rough approximation, your agent uses `figma-use` to write real, editable Figma content: the same components, variables, and layout rules your team already relies on. The result lands directly on the canvas and is ready to inspect, refine, and extend.

You can write to any Figma Design file you have edit access to. To get started, share a Figma file URL or a link to a specific selection in your prompt, then describe what you want to create or change. For example:

*   "Using this Figma file: <URL>, create a new page and build a settings screen using our existing components."
*   "Using this selection: <URL>, add an empty state that matches the existing design system."
*   "Using this Figma file: <URL>, convert the raw color values in this frame to variables."

**When to use it:** Use this skill any time you want your agent to create or modify content on the Figma canvas, whether you're building a new screen, updating components, or working with variables and tokens.

**Requirements:**

*   A Figma Design file URL or a link to a specific selection
*   Edit access to the file

### figma-use-figjam

`figma-use-figjam` is the foundational skill for working with FigJam boards. When you want your agent to create or modify content directly in a FigJam file, such as adding stickies, sections, connectors, shapes, tables, or code blocks, this is the skill that makes it possible.

Instead of treating FigJam like a generic whiteboard, your agent uses `figma-use-figjam` to work with real, editable FigJam content and structure. The result lands directly on the board and is ready to review, reorganize, and build on with your team.

You can use it with FigJam boards you have access to through a supported MCP client. To get started, share a FigJam file URL or a link to a specific board in your prompt, then describe what you want to create or change. For example:

*   "Using this FigJam file: <URL>, organize this brainstorm into sections and add stickies for the main themes."
*   "Using this FigJam board: <URL>, create a planning board with sections, stickies, and connectors for this project brief."
*   "Using this FigJam file: <URL>, update this architecture diagram with a new service and reconnect the related systems."

**When to use it:** Use this skill any time you want your agent to create or modify content on a FigJam board, whether you're organizing information, building a planning board, or refining a diagram.

**Requirements:**

*   A FigJam file URL or a link to a specific selection
*   Edit access to the file

### figma-use-slides

`figma-use-slides` is the foundational skill for working with Figma Slides decks. When you want your agent to create or modify content directly in a Slides file, such as adding slides, organizing them into sections, updating text and shapes on a slide, applying a theme, or writing speaker notes, this is the skill that makes it possible.

Instead of producing a static export or a one-off mockup, your agent uses `figma-use-slides` to write real, editable Slides content: actual slides in the slide grid, theme variables and text styles your team can keep building on, and speaker notes that show up in Presenter View. The result lands directly in the deck and is ready to present, refine, and extend.

You can use it with Slides files you have edit access to. To get started, share a Slides file URL or a link to a specific slide in your prompt, then describe what you want to create or change. For example:

*   "Using this Slides file: <URL>, build a five-slide kickoff deck for this project brief."
*   "Using this slide: <URL>, rework the layout to match the rest of the deck."
*   "Using this Slides file: <URL>, add speaker notes for every slide that has substantive content."
*   "Using this Slides file: <URL>, organize the deck into sections and name them."

**When to use it:** Use this skill any time you want your agent to create or modify content in a Slides deck, whether you're building a new presentation, reworking individual slides, or adding speaker notes.

**Requirements:**

*   A Slides file URL or a link to a specific slide
*   Edit access to the file

### figma-swiftui

`figma-swiftui` translates between Figma designs and SwiftUI code in both directions. Use it to implement a Figma design as SwiftUI in your iOS project, or to push SwiftUI views and screens back into a Figma file.

The skill recognizes iOS patterns rather than rebuilding them from primitives. A Figma frame with a large title and back chevron becomes a `NavigationStack`, and a row of icon-and-label pairs becomes a `TabView`. SF Symbols round-trip by name in both directions, and semantic colors map to the iOS HIG tokens your team already uses (`Color(.systemBackground)`, `Color.secondary`) rather than being inlined as hex values.

To get started, share a Figma file URL alongside your SwiftUI project, then describe which direction you want. For example:

*   "Implement this Figma screen in SwiftUI: <URL>"
*   "Build this in SwiftUI for iPad: <URL>"
*   "Push the SwiftUI views in `Sources/Screens/Settings/` into this Figma file: <URL>"
*   "Mirror this SwiftUI design system in Figma: <URL>"

If the request is ambiguous, such as a Figma URL appearing alongside `.swift` files with no clear verb, your agent will ask which direction you want before continuing.

**When to use it:** Use this skill any time you want to translate between a Figma design and SwiftUI code, whether you're implementing a screen for iOS or pushing existing SwiftUI views back into Figma.

**Requirements:**

*   A Figma Design file URL
*   For pushing SwiftUI into Figma, edit access to the file

### figma-code-connect

`figma-code-connect` connects your published Figma components to their matching code implementations using Figma's Code Connect feature. Once connected, developers can open a component in Figma's Dev Mode and navigate directly to the corresponding code without having to hunt for it.

To use it, point your agent at a Figma selection or share a Figma URL containing the components you want to connect. The agent will scan your codebase for matching components, show you the proposed connections for review, and then create them in bulk once you confirm.

**When to use it:** Use this skill when you want developers in Dev Mode to be able to see code references linked from the design component to its implementation in the codebase.

**Requirements:**

*   A Figma URL for the components you want to connect, or the components selected in the Figma desktop app
*   Components must be published to a team library
*   Professional, Organization, or Enterprise plan

### figma-create-new-file

`figma-create-new-file` creates a new blank Figma file in your drafts. It works for both design files and FigJam boards.

**Usage:** `/figma-create-new-file [editorType] [fileName]`

Examples:

*   `/figma-create-new-file` creates a design file named "Untitled"
*   `/figma-create-new-file figjam My Whiteboard` creates a FigJam file named "My Whiteboard"
*   `/figma-create-new-file design My New Design` creates a design file named "My New Design"

When the file is created, your agent returns a link you can open directly in Figma.

If your account belongs to multiple Figma organizations, your agent will ask which one to create the file under before proceeding.

**When to use it:** Use this skill whenever you need a fresh Figma file, typically as the first step before asking your agent to build something on the canvas with `figma-use`.

### figma-generate-diagram

`figma-generate-diagram` turns a description of a system, process, or flow into an editable FigJam diagram. Describe what you want to diagram and your agent will produce a flowchart, sequence diagram, ER diagram, state diagram, or Gantt chart, and place it in a FigJam file you can keep editing.

Instead of generating a static image you have to redraw to change, your agent uses `figma-generate-diagram` to write a real FigJam diagram: actual nodes and connectors you can move, rename, restyle, and build on with your team. For diagrams that need annotations or color-coded sections beyond what the base diagram supports, the agent can extend it with stickies, shapes, and other FigJam content after the diagram is created.

To get started, describe the diagram you want, or point your agent at the source material it should diagram, such as code, a spec, or an existing file. For example:

*   "Diagram the auth handshake between our web client, API gateway, and identity service as a sequence diagram."
*   "Using the schema in this repo, generate an ER diagram of our core tables."
*   "Create a flowchart of the onboarding steps in this PRD, and add stickies next to each step with the owning team."

**When to use it:** Use this skill when you want a diagram you can keep editing in FigJam, whether you're documenting a system, walking a team through a process, or sketching a data model.

**Requirements:**

*   A description of what to diagram, or a link to the source material the diagram should be based on

### figma-code-workflows

`figma-code-workflows` brings an existing project from your computer into Figma. Tell your agent what you want to end up with, and it picks the right tool and walks through the import:

*   **A code layer** in a Figma Design file, so your running app sits on the canvas next to your designs
*   **A standalone Figma Make file**, so you can keep building the app with the Figma Make agent
*   **Editable design layers** in a Figma Design file, captured from a running app or converted from an HTML file

If you don't say which one you want, your agent asks before it starts. Your agent keeps you updated as it prepares, uploads, and imports the project, and shares a link to the result when it's done.

For example:

*   "Import this project as a code layer in this Figma file: <URL>"
*   "Bring this app into a new Figma Make file."
*   "Turn this HTML page into editable design layers in this file: <URL>"

Imports can take 10 minutes or more. Some projects need changes to run in Figma, and your agent may need to adjust and retry the import.

**When to use it:** Use this skill when you've built something with your coding agent and want to keep iterating, collaborating, and sharing it in Figma.

**Requirements:**

*   An existing project on your computer. This skill doesn't create new apps from a description.
*   Edit access to the destination file
*   To create a code layer, a Full seat and access to code layers

### figma-spec

`figma-spec` lets your agent read, create, and update Figma Specs, whether it's a standalone spec or a spec embedded in a Figma Design or FigJam file.

Use specs to give your agent project context, like requirements, decisions, and open questions, before it starts building. As it works, your agent can capture decisions and discoveries back in the spec, so your team stays in sync. Your agent makes targeted edits instead of rewriting the whole spec, and keeps existing comments attached to the right text.

For example:

*   "Read the spec in <URL> and implement the checkout requirements."
*   "Draft a spec for the onboarding redesign in this FigJam file: <URL>"
*   "Add the edge cases we found today to the open questions section of this spec: <URL>"

**When to use it:** Use this skill when you want your agent to work from your team's requirements, or to keep a spec up to date as the work changes.

**Requirements:**

*   A link to a Figma spec, or to the Figma Design or FigJam file that contains it
*   To create or update a spec, edit access to the file

**Note:** Figma Specs is in open beta. Support for spec comment workflows is coming soon.

## Example skills: Write to canvas

`figma-generate-library` and `figma-generate-design` are examples of what's possible when you build on top of `figma-use`. Each one shows how write-to-canvas can be combined with design system awareness and multi-step orchestration to tackle a larger workflow.

Both skills are fully functional and ready to use. They're also provided as references: if you want to build your own skill for a workflow specific to your team, these are good starting points to learn from and adapt.

### figma-generate-library

`figma-generate-library` builds or updates a Figma design system library from your codebase. It works in phases: first understanding what you have (in both code and Figma), then creating token collections, building out component pages, and running a final quality check. It pauses for your review between phases before continuing.

The phases are:

*   **Discovery**: Reviews your codebase and existing Figma file to understand what tokens and components are already there, then confirms scope with you before creating anything
*   **Foundations**: Creates variable collections for colors, spacing, and other tokens; sets up text and effect styles
*   **File structure**: Sets up standard pages (Cover, Getting Started, Foundations, Components, Utilities) with documentation for color swatches, type specimens, and spacing
*   **Components**: Builds each component with variants, auto-layout, and variable bindings; validates with screenshots before moving on
*   **Integration and QA**: Finalizes Code Connect mappings, checks naming and accessibility, and takes final screenshots

**When to use it:** Use this skill when you want to generate or sync a Figma design system library from your codebase, including themes like light and dark mode, token collections, and component libraries.

**Requirements:**

*   Access to the project codebase
*   An existing Figma file to build into (create one first with `figma-create-new-file` if needed)

### figma-generate-design

`figma-generate-design` builds full-page screens in Figma using real components, variables, and styles from your design system. Point it at a page or view in your codebase and it will find the matching design system assets, import them, and assemble the screen section by section.

For web apps, it can also take a live screenshot of the running application to use as a layout reference, helping it match the real proportions and spacing.

**When to use it:** Use this skill when you want to push a page, screen, or multi-section layout from your application into Figma.

**Requirements:**

*   Access to the project codebase
*   A Figma file with a connected design system, or a linked library

URL 与 header 配置 | 粒度 | URL | header | local flag / env | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | toolset | `/mcp/x/{toolset}`（只能单个）、`/mcp/x/all` | `X-MCP-Toolsets`（可多个，逗号分隔） | `--toolsets` / `GITHUB_TOOLSETS` | | 单个 tool | — | `X-MCP-Tools`（叠加在 toolset 上） | `--tools` / `GITHUB_TOOLS` | | 排除 tool | — | `X-MCP-Exclude-Tools` | `--exclude-tools` / `GITHUB_EXCLUDE_TOOLS` | | 只读 | 后缀 `/readonly` | `X-MCP-Readonly` | `--read-only` / `GITHUB_READ_ONLY` | | lockdown | — | `X-MCP-Lockdown` | `GITHUB_LOCKDOWN_MODE` | | insiders | 后缀 `/insiders` | `X-MCP-Insiders` | `--insiders` / `GITHUB_INSIDERS` | | feature flags | 查询参数 `?features=` | `X-MCP-Features`（同时存在时 header 胜，即使为空） | `--features` / `GITHUB_FEATURES` | 容错故意不对称：无效 toolset 名静默忽略、服务照常启动；无效 tool 名报错并阻止启动。布尔 header 的假值集合固定为空、`false`、`f`、`no`、`n`、`0`、`off`（忽略空格与大小写），其余一律为真。 lockdown 是单向棘轮：服务端已开启时客户端 header 关不掉，只能冗余地再开一次；文档同时声明它是 best-effort 内容过滤，不是安全边界。 `X-MCP-Tools` 于 2025-12-10 才加入，原因是生产统计发现最高频的几个工具分属不同 toolset。分层配置不是一次设计好的。 ## 对 KITT 的映射 | GitHub 的做法 | KITT 对应 | 判断 | | --- | --- | --- | | URL 即配置：`/x/{toolset}` + `/readonly` + `/insiders` 正交组合 | 现有 `/mcp` 与 `/api/web-guide/mcp` 是雏形，但没有修饰符维度 | 借 | | read-only 只裁 tools、漏了 prompts 与 resources | KITT 若做只读入口，必须同时裁掉会驱动写动作的 skill 与资源 | 借（作为反例） | | resources 与 prompts 挂在 toolset 上随组进出 | KITT 的目录 / 章节很适合做成 resource，随检索 toolset 一起开关 | 借 | | 破坏性工具以客户端 elicitation 能力为前置，不支持就不列出 | 真机运动、系统修改类工具可按客户端是否支持确认交互来决定是否暴露 | 借 | | 双重 scope 检查：visibility + per-call 按参数改判 | 页面授权、下载授权、领域执行授权可分别做展示期与调用期两道检查 | 借 | | feature flag 替换而非追加工具 | 工具演进时避免同名不同义，用 flag 做整组切换 | 借 | | 自有逻辑全部集中在工具面治理与输出投影，数据面纯转发 | KITT 检索有真实算法（召回、融合、重排），归属更接近「自有」；网页指引更接近纯转发 | 参照分类 | | `tooldiscovery` 写了没接入 | KITT 工具数尚少，暂不需要工具搜索 | 不借 | | remote / local 双形态 | KITT 已定服务端形态，仅遥操硬件留本地 | 不借 | | insiders 通道 | 用户量不足 | 不借 | | `github_support_docs_search` 独立成 toolset | 与 KITT 检索同定位，可参照把「文档检索」与「操作类」分属不同 toolset | 参照 | 相关：[[KITT/Ref/飞书OpenAPIMCP|飞书 OpenAPI MCP]] · [[KITT/Ref/FigmaMCP|Figma MCP]] · [[KITT/架构/交付形态对比|交付形态对比]] · [[KITT/架构/网页配对与会话生命周期|网页配对与会话生命周期]] 来源：[Remote Server](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/blob/main/docs/remote-server.md)、[Server Configuration](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/blob/main/docs/server-configuration.md)、[PAT Scope Filtering](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/blob/main/docs/scope-filtering.md)、[GitHub App 鉴权](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/blob/main/docs/github-app-auth.md)、[Feature Flags](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/blob/main/docs/feature-flags.md)、[README 自动生成工具表](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/blob/main/README.md)。工具数、只读数、resources 与 prompts 数量、feature flag 替换行为均通过 `ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server` 实跑 `tools/list`、`resources/templates/list`、`prompts/list` 测得；后端归属与门控条件核对 `main` 分支源码 `pkg/github/tools.go`、`resources.go`、`prompts.go`、`find_duplicate.go`、`csv_output.go`、`repositories.go`、`pkg/inventory/tool_availability.go`、`pkg/tooldiscovery/search.go`。

--- aliases: [figma-mcp-server, FigmaMCP工具清单, FigmaMCP鉴权, FigmaSkills] --- # Figma MCP Server：能力清单与实现归属 双形态：remote（`https://mcp.figma.com/mcp`，推荐，能力最全）与 desktop（Figma 桌面应用 Dev Mode 内启用，`http://127.0.0.1:3845/mcp`）。三家里工具最多，也是唯一把 **Skills 作为一等交付物**的。 ## MCP 原语清单 | 原语 | 数量 | 说明 | | --- | --- | --- | | tools | **41** | 18 read + 14 write + 9 Weave | | prompts | **1** | `create_design_system_rules` | | resources | **0** | 未使用 MCP resources | 其中 38 个工具有独立文档小节，3 个标注 *(Figma-prompted)* 的只出现在索引表：`get_code_connect_suggestions`、`get_context_for_code_connect`、`send_code_connect_mappings`。官方原文——这些由 Figma 或 `figma-code-connect` skill 在更大工作流中调用，用户不需要直接调。 **形态差异决定工具面**：标 ✓ 的仅 remote 可用。desktop 不支持写画布、不支持发送 UI 到 Figma，且 remote 必须在 prompt 里带文件/图层链接，desktop 才能直接读当前选区。 ## Tools 全清单（按分组） 分组依据是**任务方向**，不是后端 API 域。 ### Design to code（读，7） | 工具 | 输出 | 约束 | | --- | --- | --- | | `get_metadata` | 轻量 XML 大纲：layer ID、名称、类型、位置、尺寸 | 不传 node ID 返回顶层 page 列表；**node ID 无效时错误响应里也附 page 列表** | | `get_design_context` | 结构化设计上下文 + 代码，默认 React + Tailwind | 主工具。`clientFrameworks` 指定 Code Connect 标签；Professional 同时只能一个活跃框架，Org/Enterprise 可多个 | | `get_screenshot` | PNG | 1 节点/次，仅 PNG，费 token | | `download_assets` ✓ | 导出渲染 + 原始上传图 | ≤20 节点/次；格式 PNG/JPG/SVG/PDF，缩放 0.01x–4x，无导出设置时 1x 最长边约 4096px；原始图 ≤20 张，超出返回 `rawImagesTruncated: true` | | `get_variable_defs` | 选区用到的变量与样式（颜色、间距、字体） | — | | `get_motion_context` | 关键帧轨道 + 缓动曲线 + 可直接用的 CSS `@keyframes` 与 Motion 片段 | 在 `get_design_context` 之后用同一 node ID；`recursive: true` 取选区内全部动画层 | | `get_figjam` | FigJam 图的 XML 大纲 + 节点截图 | 仅 FigJam 文件 | `get_screenshot` 与 `download_assets` 的分工被写成正文对照表：前者「需要看见」（1 节点、仅 PNG、总是重渲染），后者「需要交付」（≤20 节点、多格式、可返回原始上传文件）。 ### Code to design（写，7） | 工具 | 作用 | | --- | --- | | `use_figma` ✓ | 通用写工具，**在文件里执行 Figma Plugin API 的 JS**，覆盖 Design / FigJam / Slides / Specs | | `upload_assets` ✓ | 上传图片与 SVG 到文件（`use_figma` 自己不能加新图） | | `generate_image` ✓ | 生成图片并放入文件，消耗 Figma AI credits | | `create_new_file` ✓ | 建空白 Design / FigJam / Slides 文件 | | `generate_diagram` ✓ | 由描述或 Mermaid 语法生成 FigJam 图 | | `generate_figma_design` ✓ | 把运行中的 Web UI 转成设计图层 | | `html_to_figma` ✓ | 把 HTML 文档转成设计图层 | `use_figma` 是整个写方向的核心：agent 提交一段 Plugin API 脚本，用 `figma.closePlugin(JSON.stringify(...))` 返回结果，失败用 `figma.closePluginWithFailure()`。**它不是「一组结构化写操作」，而是一个受控的代码执行通道。** ### Design systems and Code Connect（7） | 工具 | 读/写 | 备注 | | --- | --- | --- | | `search_design_system` ✓ | 读 | 跨库搜组件、变量、样式 | | `get_libraries` ✓ | 读 | 列出已订阅与可用库 | | `get_code_connect_map` | 读 | 取选中实例的 Code Connect 映射；desktop 用 Dev Mode 里选中的映射 | | `add_code_connect_map` | 写 | 把 Figma 组件映射到代码组件 | | `get_code_connect_suggestions` | 读 | *(Figma-prompted)* | | `get_context_for_code_connect` ✓ | 读 | *(Figma-prompted)* 取 Code Connect 模板所需的组件元数据 | | `send_code_connect_mappings` | 写 | *(Figma-prompted)* 确认建议的映射 | ### Generative plugins and shaders（9） `list_generative_plugins` ✓、`get_generative_plugin` ✓、`create_generative_plugin` ✓、`update_generative_plugin` ✓、`list_shaders`、`get_shader`、`create_shader` ✓、`update_shader` ✓、`list_file_shaders` ✓。 ### Figma Make and code layers（1） `send_code_to_figma` ✓ — 把本地项目导入为 Make 文件或 code layer。首次上传不消耗 credits，后续 prompting 与修改消耗。导入可能耗时 10 分钟以上。 ### Account（1） `whoami` ✓ — 返回邮箱、所属全部计划、每个计划上的 seat 类型。**官方指定的权限诊断入口**：报权限错时第一步就是让 agent 跑它。创建 generative plugin 与 shader 需要从这里拿 `planKey`。 ### Figma Weave（9，全部 ✓） `weave_list_tools`、`weave_get_tool_inputs`、`weave_upload_asset`、`weave_run_tool`、`weave_get_tool_run_output`、`weave_cancel_tool_run`、`weave_find_model`、`weave_run_model`、`weave_get_model_run_output`。 Weave 里的「tool」指已发布的 Weave 工作流（`recipeId`），不是 MCP tool。 ### Prompts（1） `create_design_system_rules` — 无需文件。生成一份规则文件，让 agent 后续把设计转成贴合本仓库代码与设计系统的代码；官方要求把结果存进项目的 `rules/` 或 `instructions/` 目录。**这是「用 prompt 生产持久化配置」，不是会话模板。** ## 工具的后端归属 ```mermaid flowchart TB T["MCP tool call"] T --> FIG["Figma 自家服务
渲染 / 文件 API / Plugin API 运行时 / AI"] T --> WV["第三方 Weave
app.weavy.ai
独立账号 · 独立 credits"] T --> CB["用户代码库与本地项目
Code Connect 映射 · 项目导入"] T --> SVR["MCP server 自有逻辑"] FIG --> F1["读：get_design_context / get_metadata
get_screenshot / download_assets
get_variable_defs / get_motion_context / get_figjam
search_design_system / get_libraries / whoami"] FIG --> F2["写：use_figma（Plugin API 执行）
upload_assets / create_new_file
generate_image / generate_diagram
generate_figma_design / html_to_figma"] FIG --> F3["生成插件与 shader：9 个工具"] WV --> W1["weave_* 9 个
付费运行前必须两阶段确认"] CB --> C1["get/add_code_connect_map
send_code_to_figma"] SVR --> S1["输出体积上限 20KB / call"] SVR --> S2["批量上限与截断标志
rawImagesTruncated"] SVR --> S3["错误响应内嵌恢复路径
无效 node ID 附 page 列表"] SVR --> S4["按 plan × seat 限流与豁免判定"] SVR --> S5["客户端白名单准入"] ``` **唯一真正的第三方后端是 Weave**。它需要独立的付费 Weave 账号，消耗 Weave credits 而非 Figma AI credits，并且协议里内置两阶段确认： ```mermaid flowchart LR A["weave_run_model
不带 acknowledgedCost"] --> B["返回成本报价
不执行"] B --> C["agent 向用户展示成本并等确认
rerun 也要重新确认"] C --> D["weave_run_model
带 acknowledgedCost"] D --> E["执行，返回 predictionId"] E --> F["weave_get_model_run_output
weave_get_tool_run_output 轮询"] F -.-> G["weave_cancel_tool_run
不可撤销"] ``` 「用户已确认」是请求字段，不是 prompt 里的一句叮嘱，agent 跳不过去。 Figma 自己的 AI 能力（`generate_image`、向 Figma Make 发 prompt）走 Figma AI credits，**不计入 MCP rate limit**。 MCP server 自有部分全是治理：体积上限、批量截断、错误恢复信息、限流、准入。没有自有算法。 ## 鉴权与准入 | 维度 | remote | desktop | | --- | --- | --- | | 认证 | OAuth，浏览器 `Allow access` | 无独立认证，复用桌面应用会话 | | 客户端准入 | **白名单**：只有 Figma MCP catalog 列出的客户端能连，新客户端需排 waitlist | 无限制 | | seat / plan | 写画布需 Full seat（草稿外） | 需 Dev 或 Full seat + Professional / Education / Organization / Government / Enterprise | | 文件权限 | 只能操作账号已有访问权的文件 | 同 | | 企业 SSO | Claude 经 Okta Cross App Access (XAA) / OIDC，一次登录后免二次登录 | — | | 分发 | 客户端插件（含 MCP 配置 + skills + rules）或手动加 URL | Dev Mode 侧栏手动启用 | ### 限流：按 plan × seat，只对读工具计数 | seat / plan | Starter | Professional | Organization | Enterprise | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | View、Collab | 20 / 月 | 20 / 月 | 20 / 月 | 20 / 月 | | Full、Dev | — | 200 / 天，10 / 分 | 200 / 天，15 / 分 | 600 / 天，20 / 分 | Education 等同 Professional 的 Full/Dev。豁免限流的工具：`add_code_connect_map`、`create_new_file`、`generate_figma_design`、`whoami`（写类与账号类）。**限流只约束「从 Figma 读数据」的工具**，写工具改由 AI credits 与 seat 权限约束。Figma 保留随时调整的权利。 ### Figma for Government：一个现成的最小只读工具面 只支持 desktop server，只暴露 8 项：`get_screenshot`、`get_design_context`、`get_metadata`、`get_figjam`、`get_variable_defs`、`get_code_connect_map`、`add_code_connect_map`、`create_design_system_rules`。 不可用：remote server、写画布（含 `use_figma`）、发送 UI 到 Figma（含 `generate_figma_design`）、Code Connect UI（CLI 仍支持）、agent skills。文档同时明确声明 MCP 服务**未纳入 FedRAMP 审计范围**。 这是「按合规等级裁剪工具面」的完整样本：不是加只读开关，而是直接发布一份独立的受限清单，并写明审计边界。 ## 硬性工具约束 - 每次 tool call 输出上限 **20KB** - `use_figma` 不能自己加新图，需配 `upload_assets` 或 `generate_image`；不支持导入含图片/视频的组件，不支持 GIF - 字体必须已上传到 Figma 账号，仅装在本机的字体不可用 - 组件必须先手动发布，Code Connect 映射才能完成 - 写画布处于 beta，官方要求在副本或草稿文件上先试并保留备份 ## Skills：9 个官方 + 2 个示例 | skill | 作用 | 驱动的工具 | | --- | --- | --- | | `figma-use` | 写画布的基础 skill，其他 skill 依赖它 | `use_figma` | | `figma-use-figjam` | FigJam 板：stickies、sections、connectors、shapes、tables、code blocks | `use_figma` | | `figma-use-slides` | Slides：加页、分节、改文本图形、套主题、加演讲者备注 | `use_figma` | | `figma-swiftui` | Figma ↔ SwiftUI 双向；识别 iOS 模式（大标题+返回箭头 → `NavigationStack`，图标行 → `TabView`），SF Symbols 按名往返，语义色映射到 HIG token | `get_design_context`、`use_figma` | | `figma-code-connect` | 扫代码库找匹配组件，展示建议供审阅，确认后批量建映射。要求组件已发布到 team library + Professional/Org/Enterprise | 3 个 *(Figma-prompted)* 工具 | | `figma-create-new-file` | 建空白文件；多组织时先问建在哪个组织下 | `create_new_file` | | `figma-generate-diagram` | 描述或源码/PRD → 可编辑 FigJam 图（流程/时序/ER/状态/甘特） | `generate_diagram` | | `figma-code-workflows` | 把本地项目导入为 code layer / Make 文件 / 可编辑设计图层；不明确时先问 | `send_code_to_figma`、`html_to_figma`、`generate_figma_design` | | `figma-spec` | 读写 Figma Specs，做定向编辑而非整篇重写，保持评论挂在正确文本上 | `use_figma` | | `figma-generate-library`（示例） | 从代码库生成/同步设计系统库，5 阶段：Discovery → Foundations → File structure → Components → Integration & QA，**每阶段之间暂停等审阅** | `use_figma` + 依赖 `figma-use` | | `figma-generate-design`（示例） | 用真实组件、变量、样式拼整页；Web 应用可截运行图做布局参照 | `use_figma` | **分发**：客户端插件自动带（Claude Code / Cursor / Codex / VS Code / Xcode / Copilot CLI 等）；或从 `github.com/figma/mcp-server-guide` 下载 zip 手动装。手动加 MCP URL 不会带 skills。 **SKILL.md 结构**：frontmatter（`name` 小写连字符且与目录同名、`description`、可选 `compatibility` / `metadata` / `allowed-tools`）+ `# 标题` + `## When to use` + `## Instructions`（编号步骤）+ `## Examples` + `## Common edge cases`；可加 `scripts/`、`references/`、`assets/`，agent 按需加载。 官方最佳实践三条： - **description 要当路由规则写**——agent 主要靠它决定何时用这个 skill，必须说清何时用、何时不用 - **SKILL.md 保持精简**，长内容移到 `references/` - **高风险 skill 设为仅手动触发**（如 `disable-model-invocation`） skill 之间可声明硬依赖：`figma-apply-palette` 的 frontmatter 写 `compatibility: Requires the figma-use skill`，正文强制「每次调 `use_figma` 前必须先加载 `figma-use`，绝不可不加载就调」。`use_figma` 另有 `skillNames` 参数，仅用于日志、不影响执行。 错误恢复也写进 skill：`use_figma` 出错时 **STOP 不立即重试** → 调 `get_metadata` 检查残留状态、找出孤立样式 → 清理重复或半成品
